Id.description: The complete string must match the declared grammar. Reject trailing control characters and invalid bytes; never trim or normalize an identity before comparison.

Entry.description: The complete string must match the declared grammar. Reject trailing control characters and invalid bytes; never trim or normalize an identity before comparison.

Time.description: A real Gregorian UTC instant, years 0001 through 9999, with uppercase T and Z and optional one to six fractional-second digits. The pattern explicitly rejects year zero, leap seconds, offsets, local times and unsupported precision; date-time format checking also rejects impossible calendar dates. Consumers must assert the declared format. Provider-owned schemas using bare date-time retain RFC3339 syntax rather than this narrower profile.

Role.description: A permission level granted to the authenticated receiving principal for an exact resource scope. One human may hold several roles; a role does not require a separate person, organization or account. A source document or claimed actor cannot grant this role.

epoch.description: The current authority generation of this local owner. Restoring owner state changes the authority generation; an old receipt cannot silently authorize new work.

Owner.description: A local management program responsible for authorizing, remembering and recovering its accepted work. This is not the human administrator, a repository owner, a hosted account or a central domain authority. Human permission comes from the actual receiving principal and its current scoped grant.

Resource.description: The thing an operation addresses within the named owner or explicit domain context. Its identifier alone conveys neither authority nor global identity.

Repository.description: Canonical custody of source history. One repository may contain several distinct host or app entrypoints; repository identity is not host identity.

Source.description: An exact source snapshot and entrypoint used to propose a change. A Git commit or source publication is not evidence that a host or app has accepted or activated it.

Handle.description: An owner-minted reference to complete immutable bytes. Every redemption rechecks the actual receiving principal, resource, purpose and owner epoch against protected owner state; possession is not bearer authority. Only content.commit exposes an input handle. Planning binds its exact digest and identity; operation admission and accepted workflow preparation or phase input atomically pin referenced inputs before acknowledgement or effects. Unadmitted staging expiry cannot collect accepted references. Restoring owner state invalidates mutable staging and requires explicit recovery of retained bindings. Complete content size uses the interoperable integer range, while independently approved receiver capacity may explicitly reject new staging; transport chunks never impose a hidden total closure limit.

Cursor.description: Opaque owner-minted base64url continuation, bound to authenticated principal, exact query, retained traversal and owner epoch. Expiry requires an explicit restart; a cursor conveys no authority.

SchemaIdentity.description: The exact installed closed input or result schema. Digest is SHA-256 over canonical {root: uri, documents: {document URI: complete schema document}} containing the root document and every transitively referenced local document. Resolve references only from the approved installed schema set, never by fetching the URI. A caller-supplied identity does not approve a schema. Every schema document declares JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 at its root. Other dialects and nested dialect declarations reject; evaluation preserves the declared dialect and structural uniqueness semantics across references without rewriting the published documents or their identity. The supported closed subset uses static references and JSON Pointer fragments; nested schema IDs, dynamic references and unresolved targets are rejected, not approximated. A pointer fragment is empty or begins with a literal slash. Percent-decode the complete fragment once before splitting its reference tokens, then unescape ~1 and ~0 in that order. Encoded separators select nested schema positions; literal slashes in member names use ~1. Admission, cycle and expansion checks, core-wrapper inspection and value evaluation must resolve the same schema positions.

HandleBinding.description: Input staging has its own durable identity before any plan or operation acceptance. Owner-produced output binds to its accepted operation. Adoption pins the original immutable staging handle; it does not rewrite its identity or turn staging into execution.

ResultHandle.description: A committed operation output and its exact approved result schema. The handle owner and operation binding must match the enclosing Operation. The complete payload is canonical JSON; its digest and size commit those exact bytes. Result intake verifies canonical encoding before treating the payload as usable, including when an independently installed historical reader is selected. Noncanonical bytes are rejected, never silently normalized or rebound after custody commitment. The owning action catalog determines the permitted result type; a generic adapter action pins its selected method result schema in its reviewed subject. This declaration does not advertise an implemented capability.

GitRef.description: A literal full Git branch or tag reference. Source selection and independent source recovery use the same grammar and bound; revision expressions, malformed path components and ref metacharacters are rejected. The exact commit remains separately pinned.

RecordReference.description: An owner-minted immutable canonical-JSON snapshot of one complete record, independently of operation admission. The record identity, exact owner epoch, record-declared generation, installed schema closure, complete byte digest and size are inseparable. Immutable Plans use null generation; Operations, Workflows and WorkflowTransferRecords use their declared generation, with the digest distinguishing every snapshot. Possession grants no read or execution authority: every record.read rechecks the actual receiving principal and the protected snapshot resource closure. The owner commits complete retrievable snapshot custody before advertising this reference. Later generations never replace its bytes. Plan expiry affects admission, not completion of an already advertised traversal; accepted, active, uncertain and recovery-required custody cannot lose its only retrievable evidence. An explicit expired or restored snapshot requires a fresh record lookup, never silent rebinding. Accepted work must remain discoverable and fully retrievable through its current record even if old completed traversals are collected. This reference does not establish plan review, acceptance or execution success before its complete payload is verified. Size describes the record and adds no total-size limit beyond its owning contract; transfers use bounded chunks and local capacity failures must be explicit. A historical schema closure is readable only through an immutable reader independently installed by the receiver for that exact digest and the declared record-kind URI. CLI envelopes, SSH results, pages and chunks propagate the same trusted reader context; neither the record nor its caller can install a reader. Historical retrieval does not admit new work under an obsolete schema. Discovery and ResourceReport use immutable observation snapshot identities: record.id equals snapshot_id and generation is null, because neither invents a ledger generation. Discovery pins records.schema.json#/$defs/Info; ResourceReport pins resource-records.schema.json#/$defs/ResourceReport. Reassembly yields exactly the complete inline payload under that schema. Each read reauthorizes its protected disclosure scope and snapshot; later observations never change these bytes. A retained reader is selected by this exact kind URI and closure digest, not by treating an observation as an Operation. Observation and ProblemEvidence also use snapshot_id as record.id and null generation. Their record.resource is required and equals the complete payload resource. WorkflowTransferRecord also requires record.resource equal to its workflow resource, uses transfer_id as record.id and its last retained transfer generation, and pins workflow-transfer-history.schema.json#/$defs/WorkflowTransferRecord. The resource is absent for other record kinds. Observation pins records.schema.json#/$defs/Observation and preserves the observed resource generation inside its payload, without treating that value as a mutable snapshot generation. ProblemEvidence pins records.schema.json#/$defs/ProblemEvidence and retains the complete evidence selection for one exact owner/resource. Each lookup and chunk read independently checks current permission for that protected disclosure scope; an authenticated failure or possession of its evidence reference grants no additional read permission.

RecordChunk.description: One exact requested byte range from the immutable record snapshot. The complete reference and starting offset match the request; decoded bytes are at most the requested length and 196608 bytes. next_offset equals offset plus decoded length and never exceeds the pinned size. complete is true exactly at that size; a nonterminal chunk must make progress. Consumers reject substituted references, offsets, invalid base64, gaps, overlaps and premature completion, then verify complete size, digest, canonical encoding, installed schema and record identity before using the record. A chunk or an exhausted connection is not a completed record.

MaterialDigest.description: The digest of immutable material required to execute or recover the selected work, including a release, source closure, checkpoint, candidate or retained evidence record. A Plan subject value with this semantic type must occur in input_digests and remain under verified owner custody. A manifest or protected owner record also retains the material closure that it references. An identity or comparison hash alone is not custody; schema identities, expected predecessors and other integrity preconditions use Digest instead.
